summary:
This handoff covers the delivery of the **Business Service: Diagram Editing Service** (biz-service-editing) — an interactive drag-and-drop PlantUML activity diagram editor for Windows desktop. The service enables developers to create, edit, import, export, and sync PlantUML diagrams without manual environment setup or PlantUML syntax knowledge.

## Scope

**Motivation & Strategy:** The work is driven by developer need for intuitive PlantUML editing (mot-driver-need) and zero-configuration setup (mot-driver-zero), informed by current web app friction (mot-assessment-web). The strategic goal is to deliver a PlantUML Desktop Editor (mot-goal-desktop) realized through the Work Package: Port web app to Electron desktop (strat-coa-port), which establishes the Capability: Desktop PlantUML Editing (strat-capability). The expected Outcome (mot-outcome) is that developers create PlantUML diagrams via drag-and-drop on Windows.

**Principles & Requirements:** Four anchoring principles guide implementation: single-click zero-config installer (mot-principle-install), free-form canvas positioning (mot-principle-freeform), last-write-wins bidirectional sync (mot-principle-sync), and real-environment acceptance testing (mot-principle-real-env-test) which mandates that all acceptance tests must execute against the actual built Windows desktop application. Four functional requirements must be delivered: drag-and-drop Activity Diagram editing (mot-req-dragdrop), one-click export to .puml and .png (mot-req-export), import existing .puml files (mot-req-import), and bidirectional canvas-code synchronization (mot-req-sync). Three technical constraints apply: Electron + React + TypeScript stack (mot-constraint-electron), Windows-only desktop application (mot-constraint-windows), and Python backend minimal footprint limited to rendering only (mot-constraint-python-backend).

**Business Layer:** The service is realized by two business processes: Edit Diagram (biz-process-edit) — palette drag, canvas placement, connector creation, container nesting, code sync — and Export Diagram (biz-process-export) — one-click .puml and .png export. The primary business actor is the Developer (biz-actor-developer).

**Application Concerns (A–G):** Seven orthogonal concerns must be implemented:
- **A: AST Data Model** — TypeScript types for all PlantUML activity diagram elements, container nesting, serialization/deserialization
- **B: ReactFlow Canvas Engine** — free-form canvas with custom node renderers, drag-and-drop, connection handles
- **C: Ace Code Editor Wrapper** — syntax highlighting, line markers, debounced change events (200ms)
- **D: Bidirectional Sync Engine** — last-write-wins conflict resolution, fingerprint matching, version tracking
- **E: PlantUML Parser and Generator** — stack-based parser, depth-tracked generator, tolerance for unsupported features
- **F: Component Palette** — left-panel draggable items in Flow/Structure/Decoration categories
- **G: Electron Desktop Shell** — main process, native menus, file dialogs, subprocess management for Python backend, first-launch downloads, auto-updater

Concern G serves all other concerns (A–F). Concern A provides types for B and E. Concerns B, C, and E connect to D for synchronization. D also updates C (code editor).

**Technology Stack:** The implementation must use Electron (tech-electron) with React 18+ + TypeScript + Vite (tech-react-ts) for the renderer, ReactFlow (tech-reactflow) for canvas, Ace Editor (tech-ace) for code editing, Node.js (tech-nodejs) for main process, JRE jlink minimal ~40MB (tech-jre) for PlantUML rendering, Python Render Backend via PyInstaller (tech-python-backend) for SVG/PNG rendering, PlantUML JAR ~20MB (tech-plantuml-jar), NSIS Installer Artifact (tech-installer) via electron-builder, and Windows PC (tech-windows-pc) as the target device.

## What Implementation Must Produce

1. A self-contained Windows desktop application (.exe installer via NSIS) that:
   - Runs as standalone without browser, Python, Java, or .env setup
   - Downloads JRE (~40MB) and PlantUML JAR (~20MB) on first launch
   - Provides drag-and-drop editing of PlantUML Activity Diagrams
   - Synchronizes canvas and code editor bidirectionally (200ms debounce, last-write-wins)
   - Allows importing existing .puml files with default grid layout
   - Allows exporting to .puml (logical structure) and .png (rendered via PlantUML)
2. TypeScript AST data model as the foundation for all diagram editing logic
3. Python backend reduced to only /render (SVG) and /renderPNG endpoints
4. All ~40 legacy PlantUML manipulation endpoints replaced by TypeScript AST
5. Acceptance test cases defined in the intent graph must pass (see each element's testcases)

## Key Architecturally Significant Boundaries

- Free-form canvas positioning: PlantUML auto-layout is NOT used for editing; .puml export contains logical structure only (no positional data)
- Canvas-code sync: Last-write-wins by timestamp; fingerprint matching preserves element positions across re-parses
- ContainerNode abstraction supports nesting via children array
- Unrecognized PlantUML features shown as grey read-only blocks on import
- Python backend lifecycle: spawned on first export, health-check polling, graceful shutdown within 3s of SIGTERM

openQuestions.question: What DPI/resolution should the .png export use?
openQuestions.recommendedAnswer: Use PlantUML's default output resolution (96 DPI) initially, with no user-configurable option for MVP. This matches the web app's existing behavior.
openQuestions.reason: The requirement (mot-req-export) specifies 'one-click export' implying no configuration dialog. Keeping 96 DPI avoids UI complexity. A future enhancement could add a resolution picker.

openQuestions.question: How are element positions preserved across .puml re-import when the .puml format does not store positional data?
openQuestions.recommendedAnswer: Use a companion sidecar file (e.g., `.puml.meta` JSON) stored alongside the .puml file that maps element fingerprints to canvas positions. When the sidecar is missing, fall back to default grid layout.
openQuestions.reason: TC-D-2 requires fingerprint matching to preserve positions. A sidecar file is the simplest way to persist positions without polluting the .puml format. The fingerprint is computed from the element's text content (type + label + nesting path).

openQuestions.question: Should the application support opening multiple diagrams in tabs, or is single-window single-diagram sufficient for MVP?
openQuestions.recommendedAnswer: Single-window single-diagram for MVP. Multi-tab support adds significant complexity to Concern G (Electron shell window management) and can be added post-MVP.
openQuestions.reason: No requirement in the intent graph specifies multi-tab support. The business processes (Edit Diagram, Export Diagram) assume a single active diagram. Delaying multi-tab avoids scope creep.

openQuestions.question: What is the expected behavior when the user edits code in a way that creates a syntactically invalid PlantUML diagram?
openQuestions.recommendedAnswer: The parser (Concern E) should handle partial/syntactically-invalid states gracefully: show unrecognized features as grey read-only blocks (same as TC-REQ-IM-1 behavior). The canvas should still display whatever was last successfully parsed. Do not block code edits due to parse errors.
openQuestions.reason: The requirements (TC-REQ-SYNC-1, TC-E-1/2) describe sync behavior during editing, but do not specify error recovery. Graceful degradation to read-only display for invalid portions is consistent with the import tolerance pattern.

openQuestions.question: What testing framework and approach should the implementation team use?
openQuestions.recommendedAnswer: Use Vitest for unit tests (TypeScript-native, Vite-compatible) and Playwright for E2E tests (Electron support) targeting the real built Electron app on Windows 10/11. Acceptance tests defined in the intent graph MUST run as Playwright E2E tests against the actual built Windows desktop application (mot-principle-real-env-test). Unit tests with mocked Electron/Node APIs are acceptable for lower-level Concerns A (AST) and E (Parser/Generator), but all acceptance-level testcases must execute in a real app instance.
openQuestions.reason: The principle mot-principle-real-env-test (Real-environment acceptance testing) mandates that all acceptance tests execute against the actual built Windows desktop application. Playwright has first-class Electron support for real-environment testing. The tech stack (Vite) makes Vitest the natural unit test choice for non-acceptance testing.

openQuestions.question: What is the auto-update mechanism for delivering new versions to users?
openQuestions.recommendedAnswer: Use electron-updater (from electron-builder) with GitHub Releases as the update source. This is the standard approach for Electron + electron-builder workflows. Implement auto-check on startup with a user notification and optional download.
openQuestions.reason: Concern G (Electron Desktop Shell) mentions 'auto-updater' in its description, but no requirement defines it. electron-updater is the de facto standard for electron-builder distributions and integrates seamlessly with NSIS installers.

notes: All acceptance testcases defined in the intent graph elements must be implemented as executable tests. Each element's testcases (TC-*) are listed under its 'testcases' array in SystemArchitecture.json.

The implementation stage must produce an Implementation Architecture (OVERALL_ARCHITECTURE.md + local ARCHITECTURE.md per stable directory) before any coding begins. See .opencode/skills/ for stage workflows.
The Python backend must NOT retain any of the ~40 legacy manipulation endpoints. Only /render (SVG) and /renderPNG endpoints are permitted.
The first-launch download flow (JRE + PlantUML JAR) is critical for the zero-config promise. Ensure progress indication and error handling are robust, as this is the user's first impression.
The Bidirectional Sync Engine (Concern D) must guard against infinite sync loops. The 200ms debounce and timestamp-based last-write-wins are mandatory safeguards.

The .puml export must NOT embed positional/CSS data. If a sidecar file (.puml.meta) is used for positions, it must be explicitly named and documented so users understand it is not part of standard PlantUML.

All technology components listed should be validated against the constraint that the Electron renderer process runs the React app, the main process handles native APIs, and subprocess management spawns Python/PyInstaller only when rendering is triggered.
The NSIS installer must install to Program Files by default, create desktop and Start Menu shortcuts, and provide a clean uninstall path. See TC-TECH-INST-1 for acceptance criteria.
This handoff was generated from design/KG/SystemArchitecture.json. Any subsequent changes to the intent graph should trigger a new handoff.

CRITICAL: Principle mot-principle-real-env-test (Real-environment acceptance testing) mandates that ALL acceptance tests MUST execute against the actual built Windows desktop application (Electron + React) on a real Windows 10/11 environment. Architecture tests must validate behavior on a real Windows instance. Unit tests with mocked Electron/Node APIs are acceptable only for sub-acceptance-level testing (e.g., Concerns A and E). Playwright E2E is the recommended approach for real-environment acceptance testing.
All new or modified acceptance testcases must be written as Playwright E2E tests targeting the built Electron app, not simulated/headless/mock environments.
